A new report

Capture the finding. Keep the evidence. Share what is useful.

From draft to report

  1. Describe what you observed.
  2. Link the original source and fixed version.
  3. Distinguish support claims from tests.
  4. Export the Markdown file.
  5. Add it to reports/, rebuild and deploy when ready.

Drafts are saved in this browser. Export a copy to keep it elsewhere. Saving does not publish your report.

The approach

Evidence before enthusiasm.

A small library with a clear paper trail.

AI Skill Library collects useful workflows for building websites, making videos, writing code, managing context, researching and engineering skills. Reports explain the choices behind the collection.

Three evidence levels

Official static evidence means a pinned official Codex source and its metadata were inspected. It describes documentary verification.

Upstream claims support means the source explicitly mentions Codex. This library has not executed the workflow.

Unknown compatibility means the inspected material does not establish Codex support.

Read the source before you use it

Every entry records a purpose, source URL, fixed commit, file manifest, license evidence and dependencies. The installer verifies downloaded file hashes. Some entries require a full upstream plugin and are unavailable through standalone copying.

Reports, kept by hand

The discovery snapshot is preserved with its collection errors. New articles record sources, limitations and practical conclusions. No recurring report schedule is configured.
